pairs.why: B is mostly saturated teal water with warm wood, like the real card's water-led palette. A gives a large flat sky-blue area the real card lacks.
Both use the same saturated orange sand, the same red, blue and green panels and the same purple cap. Neither is closer on hue or chroma.
B stays with blue steel and a pastel blue and pink sky. A adds a pink floor, a lime plant and an orange bench, which is more hue families than the real card has.
B's background is a slightly richer orange-yellow glow, closer to the real card. A's is paler. Both put cream keys on a navy body where the real keys are blue.
A has deeper red canopy undersides and a slightly darker, more saturated blue at the edges. B's cyan is brighter and the whole card is lighter.
B keeps a restrained green and white palette with a cool blue tint. A adds an orange cushion, a lime plant and red and blue books, so it has more hue families and louder accents than the real card.
A's rope is a richer saturated gold-orange against the purple, as the real objects are. B's rope is paler.
Both ropes are the same gold on the same purple with a small red accent. Neither differs enough in color to choose.
